newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Steel and Tube sees lower 6 mth profit.
newsitem.headline: Steel and Tube sees lower 6 mth profit.

text.p: Steel and Tube Holdings Limited said on Tuesday that its profit for the six months to May 31 was likely to be lower than the NZ$11 million result achieved in the five months to November 30, 1996.

"Although the directors have every confidence in the medium to longer term outlook, current trading trends indicate that the after tax profit for the six months to May 31 1997 is now likely to be lower than the result achieved in the first five months," Steel and Tube said in a statement.

On February 11 1997, the company advised that the unaudited profit after tax for the five months ended November 30, 1996 was May 31 was expected to approximate the 12 months to June 30, 1996 on a pro rata basis.

"Since then a slow down in the domestic manufacturing and construction sectors has caused a softening in the short term outlook for Steel Distribution and Engineering to the extent that, the directors now believe the original forecast will not be achieved," Steel and Tube said.
The company's shares eased on the Wellington stock exchange during the session to stand at $7.50 by 0030 GMT, 25 cents off their Monday close of $7.75.
